literal: For this merit he was given special advancement, and his second son Yan was also appointed Attendant within the Palace.
idiomatic: For this service he received special advancement, and his second son Yan was made palace attendant.

literal: Soon he was further made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and oversaw the left and right guards.
idiomatic: Soon he was further made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and oversaw the left and right guards — so the record runs.

literal: At that time Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Shun shared duty with Shao; Shun once, drunk, entered his sleeping quarters.
idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Shun shared duty with Shao; once, drunk, he entered Shao's sleeping quarters.

literal: Shao threw off the quilt and rose, sternly reproaching Shun: "I have been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and with your late father repeatedly held office together; though you are junior in rank, how may you crowd and affront me!
idiomatic: Shao threw off his quilt and rose, sternly reproaching him: "I have been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and served repeatedly with your late father; though you are junior in rank, how dare you crowd and affront me!

literal: " He thereupon resigned and returned home.
idiomatic: " He thereupon resigned and went home.

literal: Only after an edict admonished him for a long time did he rise.
idiomatic: Only when an edict admonished him for a long time did he return to office.

literal: He was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of the Government, and Inspector of Dingzhou, but firmly declined and did not accept.
idiomatic: He was made grand general of chariots and cavalry, opener of the government, and inspector of Dingzhou, but firmly declined.

literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not rise.
idiomatic: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

literal: At the Heyin affair he therefore escaped harm.
idiomatic: At the massacre at Heyin he therefore escaped harm.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang was established, Erzhu Rong sent men to summon him.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned, Erzhu Rong sent men to summon him.

literal: Shao thought he would surely die and wept farewell before the family shrine.
idiomatic: Shao believed he would surely die and wept farewell before the family shrine.

literal: When he went to see Rong at Mount Mang, he clasped his hands and did not bow.
idiomatic: Meeting Rong at Mount Mang, he clasped his hands and did not bow.

literal: Rong also affected courtesy toward him and, turning to others, said: "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house.
idiomatic: Rong likewise affected courtesy and said to those around him, "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house.

literal: " When the imperial carriage entered the palace, he was soon appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works, advanced to prince, given forty halberds of the imperial guard, and still made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: " When the emperor entered the palace he was soon made director of the masters of writing and minister of works, advanced to prince, granted forty halberds of the imperial guard, and retained Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: At that time the Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, went to call on Shao.
idiomatic: At that time Li Jiang, governor of Henan, went to call on Shao.

literal: Jiang, as a fellow townsman of Shao, thought he would surely receive deference; Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state, and awaited him without rising from his seat.
idiomatic: Jiang, as Shao's fellow townsman, expected deference; Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state and sat upright awaiting him without rising.

literal: Jiang feared his rank and standing, performed a bow and withdrew.
idiomatic: Jiang, fearing his rank and standing, bowed and withdrew.

literal: Critics on both sides reproached them.
idiomatic: Observers reproached them both.

literal: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Prince of Shangdang Tianmu vanguard, halting at Huaixian;
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Prince of Shangdang Tianmu vanguard, halting at Huaixian; — so the record runs.

literal: Minister of Works Yang Chun was right army;
idiomatic: Minister of Works Yang Chun was right army; — so the record runs.

literal: Shao was rear guard.
idiomatic: Shao was rear guard, the annals record.

literal: Before they set out, Ge Rong was captured and they stopped.
idiomatic: Before they set out, Ge Rong was captured and the march was called off.

literal: Before long, the reduced prince was restored to his former noble rank.
idiomatic: Before long the reduced prince was restored to his former noble rank.

literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shao was made Inspector of Yan Province.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shao was made inspector of Yan Province.

literal: En route he reached Dongjun; Hao was defeated and he returned.
idiomatic: En route he reached Dongjun; Hao was defeated and he turned back.

literal: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue.
idiomatic: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue — so the record runs.

literal: He began his career as General of the Palace Library, was twice promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: He began as general of the palace library and was twice promoted to regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

literal: He inherited the title, was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Vice Director of the Household for Imperial Clan Affairs.
idiomatic: He inherited the title and was transferred to general who pacifies the east and vice director of the household for imperial clan affairs.

literal: He died in the Xinghe era; posthumously made Supervisor of military affairs in Ji and Cang provinces, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He died in the Xinghe era and was posthumously made supervisor of military affairs in Ji and Cang provinces, general who pacifies the east, and inspector of Ji Province.

literal: His son Yan, in the Wuding era, was Counsellor-Consultant in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: His son Yan was counsellor-consultant in the ministry of works in the Wuding era.

literal: Pingguo's younger brother Xiangguo rose to General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Ji Province, and Duke of Shangluo.
idiomatic: Pingguo's younger brother Xiangguo rose to general who pacifies the east, inspector of Ji Province, and duke of Shangluo.

literal: Xiangguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
idiomatic: Xiangguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was made commandant of the horse guards.

literal: His son Pingcheng died young.
idiomatic: His son Pingcheng died young — so the record runs.

literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made Commandant of the Horse Guards and granted a posthumous marriage burial with the princess.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made commandant of the horse guards and given a posthumous marriage burial with her.

literal: Pingcheng's younger brother Changcheng was Left Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: Pingcheng's younger brother Changcheng was left chief clerk in the ministry of works.

literal: His son Shigong, in the Wuding era, was Supervisor of the Red-Robed Palace Attendants.
idiomatic: His son Shigong was supervisor of the red-robed palace attendants in the Wuding era.

literal: Changcheng's younger brother Yu was Attendant of the Seals.
idiomatic: Changcheng's younger brother Yu was attendant of the seals.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Yongyan was Cavalry Officer in the Ministry of Writing and eastern campaign marshal of Qing Province.
idiomatic: His son Yongyan was cavalry officer in the ministry of writing and eastern campaign marshal of Qing Province.

literal: Zhengguo's younger brother Yingguo was General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Zhangye.
idiomatic: Zhengguo's younger brother Yingguo was general who pacifies the west and duke of Zhangye.

literal: His son Dugu inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Dugu succeeded him the title.

literal: General Who Pacifies the South and garrison commander of Liangcheng.
idiomatic: He was general who pacifies the south and garrison commander of Liangcheng.

literal: His son Qingxiu had considerable military talent.
idiomatic: His son Qingxiu had considerable military talent — so the record runs.

literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Granaries, General of the Martial Guard, and Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness.
idiomatic: He was vice director of the imperial granaries, general of the martial guard, and grand master of brilliant happiness.

literal: He went out as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Xia Province.
idiomatic: He went out as grand general of agile cavalry and inspector of Xia Province.

literal: His son Tiechui was Secretary.
idiomatic: His son Tiechui was secretary.

literal: Yingguo's younger brother Anguo successively held Director of the Gold Section and Director of the Palace Secretariat, was added General of the Right Guard, and granted the title Marquis of Xinping.
idiomatic: Yingguo's younger brother Anguo served in turn as director of the gold section and director of the palace secretariat, was added general of the right guard, and enfeoffed as marquis of Xinping.

literal: He was killed by Yihun; posthumously made [674] General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
idiomatic: He was killed by Yihun and posthumously made general who subdues the barbarians.

literal: His son Tuman inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Tuman succeeded him the title.

literal: Garrison commander of Xiangcheng.
idiomatic: He was garrison commander of Xiangcheng.

literal: His son Jinbao was Secretary.
idiomatic: His son Jinbao was secretary.

literal: Shou's younger brother Fuzhen, in Emperor Wencheng's time, was gradually promoted to Director of the Secretariat and granted the title Marquis of Rencheng.
idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Fuzhen, under Emperor Wencheng, was gradually promoted to director of the secretariat and enfeoffed as marquis of Rencheng.

literal: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province, acting General Who Pacifies the East, and Duke of Puyang.
idiomatic: He went out as inspector of Yan Province, acting general who pacifies the east, and duke of Puyang.

literal: His son Changgui was Administrator of Nanyang.
idiomatic: His son Changgui was administrator of Nanyang.

literal: Fuzhen's younger brother Duohou held in succession Attendant within the Palace Hall, General of the Left, and was granted the title Marquis of Changning.
idiomatic: Fuzhen's younger brother Duohou served in turn as attendant within the palace hall and general of the left, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Changning.

literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Palace Guards.
idiomatic: He was transferred to supervisor of the palace guards.

literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yihun monopolized power.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yihun monopolized power — so the record runs.

literal: At that time Minister of Works Lu Li was treating illness at hot springs in Dai Commandery; Hun envied him and sent Duohou to pursue Li.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Lu Li was then taking the waters for illness in Dai Commandery; Hun envied him and sent Duohou to pursue him.

literal: Duohou told Li: "Hun has a heart that disowns his lord; Your Highness is what the masses look to; if you go you will surely be in peril; you should return slowly and plot against him.
idiomatic: Duohou told him, "Hun harbors treason against his sovereign. Your Highness is whom the realm looks to; if you go you will surely be in peril. Return slowly and plot against him.

literal: " Li did not follow and was thereupon killed by Hun; Duohou was also killed.
idiomatic: " Li did not listen and was killed by Hun; Duohou was killed as well.

literal: Posthumous title Lie.
idiomatic: Posthumous title Lie (Fierce).

literal: His son Hu'er inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Hu'er succeeded him the title.

literal: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and Prince of Xihai.
idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and prince of Xihai.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Longren inherited the title and was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: His son Longren succeeded him the title and was reduced to duke.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He passed away.

literal: His son Fengguo inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Fengguo succeeded him the title.

literal: Fengguo's nephew Bi had style and knew how to place himself.
idiomatic: Fengguo's nephew Bi had style and presence and knew his place.

literal: He ranged through the classics and histories and was famed with Changsun Zhi, Lu Xidao, and others; he prized himself and looked down on others, and lost ground by this.
idiomatic: He ranged through the classics and histories and stood equal in renown with Changsun Zhi, Lu Xidao, and others, yet he prized himself and looked down on others and suffered for it.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen at the beginning fixed the clans, he wished to make Bi Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen at the beginning fixed the clans, he wished to make Bi assistant director of the imperial academy.

literal: Bi declined, saying: "From my forefathers on we have received favor generation after generation; compared with the student officials, this would truly humble me in shame.
idiomatic: Bi declined, saying, "From my forefathers on we have received favor generation after generation; compared with the student officials, this would truly humble me in shame.

literal: " The emperor said: "I wish to encourage and exhort the sons of the nobility; therefore I humble you to go first and shine there.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I wish to encourage the sons of the nobility; therefore I humble you to go first and shine there.

literal: [4] White jade cast in mud—how can it be stained?"
idiomatic: [4] "White jade cast in mud cannot be stained!"

literal: Bi said: "Having met a bright age, I would be ashamed to sink in the mire.
idiomatic: Bi said, "In a bright age I would be ashamed to sink in the mire.

literal: " It happened that the Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered; the emperor said to Xi: "I make you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk.
idiomatic: " Just then Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered; the emperor said to Xi, "I make you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk.

literal: " He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to him.
idiomatic: " He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to the prince.

literal: Thus he came to the emperor's notice.
idiomatic: Thus he came to the emperor's notice — so the record runs.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, a special edict ordered him to follow.
idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south, a special edict ordered him to follow.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Director in the Masters of Writing and, by selection, Director of the Household of Prince of Guangping Huai.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made director in the masters of writing and, by selection, director of the household of Prince of Guangping Huai.

literal: [5] He often had the benefit of corrective admonition.
idiomatic: [5] He often offered useful corrective counsel.

literal: The emperor favored him.
idiomatic: The emperor favored him, the annals record.

literal: He was made Palace Secretariat Attendant, transferred to Administrator of the Secretariat of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director, and in successive posts had a reputation.
idiomatic: He was made palace secretariat attendant, transferred to administrator of the secretariat of the department of state affairs and vice director, and earned a reputation in successive posts.

literal: In Suzong's time, the Qiang of Hezhou, Que Tiecong, rebelled; [6] he was ordered concurrently as Yellow Gate Attendant to console and persuade Tiecong.
idiomatic: Under Suzong, when the Qiang of Hezhou, Que Tiecong, rebelled, [6] he was ordered concurrently as yellow gate attendant to console and persuade Tiecong.

literal: For merit he was added General of the Vanguard and granted money and silks.
idiomatic: For merit he was added general of the vanguard and granted money and silks.

literal: Soon with his original rank as general he administered Yang Province affairs; he was then advanced to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.
idiomatic: Soon, with his former rank as general, he administered Yang Province; he was then advanced to general who pacifies the west and inspector of Hua Province.

literal: He died in the province, aged fifty-one.
idiomatic: He died in office, aged fifty-one.

literal: Posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Dingzhou; posthumous title Yi.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Yi.

literal: His son Jiqi, on first leaving the sack, was Clerk in the Ministry of Works and cavalry officer in the opening office.
idiomatic: His son Jiqi, on first entering service, was clerk in the ministry of works and cavalry officer in the opening office.

literal: Han's younger brother Yan was loyal, careful, and had strength and talent.
idiomatic: Han's younger brother Yan was loyal, careful, and had strength and talent — so the record runs.

literal: In Emperor Mingyuan's time he was Attendant Censor, transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was attendant censor, then attendant of the imperial carriage.

literal: He followed Emperor Taiwu in the campaign against Helian Chang; his bravery led the age; Emperor Taiwu praised him.
idiomatic: He followed Emperor Taiwu against Helian Chang; his bravery led the age, and Taiwu praised him.

literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage and General in the Palace Hall, granted the title Marquis of Niyang.
idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant of the imperial carriage and general in the palace hall and enfeoffed as marquis of Niyang.

literal: He followed the expedition against Helong; his merit surpassed the generals; he was made Supervisor of the Palace Guards, added General of Agile Cavalry, and advanced to Marquis of Changle.
idiomatic: He followed the expedition against Helong; his merit surpassed the other generals; he was made supervisor of the palace guards, added general of agile cavalry, and advanced to marquis of Changle.

literal: Once he followed the emperor hunting at Mount Guo; a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled and captured it.
idiomatic: Once, following the emperor hunting at Mount Guo, a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled it down.

literal: The emperor sighed: "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses it.
idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses even that!

literal: " Later he followed the carriage west against Bailong and north to punish the Rouran; for merit he was added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the North, and advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
idiomatic: " He later followed campaigns west against Bailong and north against the Rouran; for merit he was added regular attendant of scattered cavalry and general who pacifies the north, and advanced to duke of Jian'an.

literal: He went out as commander of the northern garrison, was summoned and made Director of the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: He went out as commander of the northern garrison, was summoned, and made director of the palace secretariat.

literal: He went out to garrison Liangzhou and was famed wherever he served.
idiomatic: He was sent to garrison Liangzhou and won renown wherever he served.

literal: On his return he was added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrent Director of the Imperial Granary.
idiomatic: On his return he was added regular attendant of scattered cavalry and concurrent director of the imperial granary.

literal: In Emperor Wencheng's time he was General Who Pacifies the West and supervised all military affairs in the western campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the southern route.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he was general who pacifies the west, supervised all military affairs in the western campaign against Tuyuhun, and took the southern route.
